population.label: Caucasian (European background; used for Australian patients of European background)

extractedBy: Task 6 AI reader A and AI reader B (mcnamara1984.a/.b, Table I rows)
curation.notes: Ruling P23: one set per McNamara sample. Ruling P24: mcnamara1984-caucasian.a.json is not an independent copy (it copied another extraction) and was not used; the Table I rows of mcnamara1984-caucasian.b.json were compared row by row against the two independent Task 6 extractions mcnamara1984.a.json and mcnamara1984.b.json, which typed Table I for the analysis's own set (script comparison 2026-10-08, positive control: two planted changes found). Result: 26 rows compared with Task 6 b, 0 differences; 24 with Task 6 a, 0 differences, a lacking SNA (2 rows). SNA checked on the page (Table I, p. 451, PDF p. 3): 82.4 ± 3.0 / 83.9 ± 3.2 -> kept. Facial axis: printed 0.2° / 0.5° (difference from 90°) -> 90.2 / 90.5 (owner ruling 7 Oct); definitionMatch same (Task 6 a and caucasian.b) over close (Task 6 b), as in the committed McNamara own set. Incisor distances close (facial surface, M1). Selection class-I-balanced: 111 young adults with good to excellent faces, Class I occlusion, good skeletal balance and a straight (orthognathic) profile (pp. 450-451). Band [18, 40] (P18): the paper gives only mean ages (women 26 y 8 m, men 30 y 9 m). Scale enlarged 8% (p. 451).

caveats: 'Caucasian' is our label: the paper never states the samples' ethnicity (it says nothing about ancestry).

Sample: 111 untreated young adults (73 women, 38 men) of Ann Arbor, Michigan, chosen by McNamara and co-workers for good to excellent facial configurations, Class I occlusion, good skeletal balance and an orthognathic profile (pp. 450-451). Only mean ages are given (women 26 y 8 m, men 30 y 9 m); the 18-40 band is the convention for adults (P18).

8% film enlargement: p. 451 says the measures from all these samples include an 8% enlargement wherever possible; the table heading says 'standardized 8% enlargement'. The app shows mm values at true size (÷ 1.08) with the printed value.
These are the Ann Arbor sample's own statistics; McNamara's composite clinical norms (Table II) are the separate analysis-own set mcnamara1984.
Incisor distances (upper incisor to A vertical, lower incisor to A-Po) are measured from the facial surface (M1), so they are close.
